evidence.quote: finding PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.’s (PJM) Tariff unjust and unreasonable

summary.short: FERC order (Docket EL25-49) on rehearing and PJM compliance. Sustains finding that PJM's Tariff lacks clear co-location rules; sets replacement transmission services (Interim NITS, firm and non-firm contract demand) for Eligible Customers serving Co-Located Load or load with BTMG; directs further PJM compliance filings within 60 days.
summary.long: Order of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, issued June 18, 2026, on rehearing, clarification, PJM's second compliance filing and the paper hearing that followed the December 18, 2025 show-cause order (193 FERC ¶ 61,217). It sustains the finding that PJM's Tariff is unjust and unreasonable for lacking clear provisions on Co-Location Arrangements, where a generator and load share a site, and for not offering transmission services that reflect a load's willingness to limit its withdrawals. It sets as just and reasonable three new transmission services for Eligible Customers serving Co-Located Load or load with behind-the-meter generation (BTMG): Interim NITS, Firm Contract Demand (FCD) and Non-Firm Contract Demand (NFCD) service, charged on contract demand. It finds PJM's retail BTMG netting rules remain unjust and unreasonable and directs revisions, including a transition period, grandfathering, and an exemption for certain cogeneration Qualifying Facilities integrated with load. It states that states keep authority over generator siting and retail cost allocation, while wholesale sales and transmission charges fall under FERC jurisdiction. It denies or dismisses most rehearing and clarification requests and directs PJM and PJM transmission owners to file further compliance filings within 60 days of the order's date.

notes: Part 1 of 4 covers the caption through p. 78 (Part IV.C.1.c.i). Only relations, entities and notes were requested; other sections are outside this part. The caption lists Docket EL25-20-001 (consolidated) while the text cites EL25-20-000 for the Constellation complaint. Many rehearing arguments on the new transmission services are dismissed as non-final because the rates, terms and conditions are set for paper hearing, so the new service terms are not final in this part. Several Industrials and Exelon/FirstEnergy requests are dismissed as outside scope or insufficiently specific. PJM's 2024 Guidance Document was rescinded and is referred to only as non-binding guidance. Part 2 of 4 covers the rehearing and compliance discussion on BTMG netting, cogeneration QFs, transmission services, Necessary Studies, Co-Located Load definition and the informational report. Only relations and entities are coded here; thresholds, obligations and deadlines in this part are left to the other parts. The order accepts and rejects PJM's compliance proposals in part, and party positions summarised here come from pleadings, not Commission findings. Entries for Exelon and FirstEnergy share one quote. Empty target_instrument_id means the target is not in the registry. Part 3 of 4 covers the compliance determinations in Part V (from the Co-Located Load definition through the penalty-charge briefs) and the paper-hearing determinations in Part VI through the start of section VI.D. Only relations and entities are annotated here; obligations, thresholds and events in this part are left to the full annotation. The December Order (193 FERC ¶ 61,217) is cited throughout but is not part of this document, so its registry ID is unknown and target_instrument_id is left empty. Footnote 724 states that the Co-Located Generating Facility definition in Tariff § I.1 does not include the language the order rejects, while the body of the order directs removal of that language from the Part III definition. The relations and entities sections are populated, so their section_status entries are set only to satisfy the schema. Part 4 of 4 covers Part VI penalty subparts (a)-(c), anti-toggling, communications, curtailment, Interim NITS, effective date, annual report, Part K, the ordering paragraphs, the Tariff appendix, the caption and Commissioner Chang's concurrence. Legal basis and the Eligible Customer definition in other parts are not coded here. The Commission finds unreserved use penalties should go to all non-offending transmission customers, which departs from the Indicated TOs proposal to distribute them to NITS and FCD customers only. The June 1, 2029 effective date is not set; PJM is directed to reconsider it. Footnote 1159 cites a proclamation that is not an operative provision. Many other citations are incidental and not coded.

evidence.quote: we direct PJM to reconsider its proposed effective date of June 1, 2029

obligations.summary: An Eligible Customer is not required to take the new transmission services and may elect NITS instead; LSEs are not required to become Eligible Customers for Co-Located Load.

evidence.quote: an Eligible Customer is not required to take the new transmission services and may elect to take NITS

obligations.summary: Ordering paragraphs (C) to (H) direct PJM and the PJM transmission owners to submit compliance filings within 60 days of the order revising the Tariff as described in the order's parts.
obligations.applies_from: within 60 days of the date of issuance of this order

evidence.quote: (C) PJM is hereby directed to submit, within 60 days of the date of issuance of this order, a compliance filing with revisions to its Tariff

enforcement.authority: PJM (as transmission provider) under its Tariff, as directed by the Commission
enforcement.triggered_by: Second instance of failing to follow a curtailment or load shedding directive by an Eligible Customer taking Interim NITS, FCD or NFCD transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Termination of the transmission service agreement with the Eligible Customer (non-monetary)
enforcement.penalty_formula: Not monetary; termination of the transmission service agreement on the second instance. The Eligible Customer may still take service for other Eligible Loads under other agreements.

evidence.quote: after the second instance of failing to follow a curtailment or load shedding directive, PJM will terminate the transmission service agreement

enforcement.authority: PJM (as transmission provider) under its Tariff, as directed by the Commission
enforcement.triggered_by: First misoperation of necessary control technologies and/or protection systems by an Eligible Customer taking Interim NITS, FCD and/or NFCD transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Suspension in service for a period of up to 120 days (non-monetary)
enforcement.penalty_formula: Not monetary; suspension of service for up to 120 days after the first misoperation.
enforcement.cure_period: Service may resume following PJM's approval, as well as the relevant transmission owner's approval of the necessary control technologies and/or protection systems

evidence.quote: an operational penalty of suspension in service for a period of up to 120 days

enforcement.authority: PJM (as transmission provider) under its Tariff, as directed by the Commission
enforcement.triggered_by: Second misoperation of necessary control technologies and/or protection systems pertaining to a transmission service agreement governing an Eligible Customer taking Interim NITS, FCD and/or NFCD transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Termination of the transmission service agreement (non-monetary)
enforcement.penalty_formula: Not monetary; termination of the specific transmission service agreement on the second misoperation. The Eligible Customer may take service on behalf of other loads under other agreements.

evidence.quote: after the second misoperation of necessary control technologies and/or protection systems, PJM will terminate the transmission service agreement

enforcement.authority: PJM transmission owners (compliance filing directed by the Commission)
enforcement.triggered_by: Unreserved use: an Eligible Customer taking any of the new transmission services on behalf of Eligible Load withdraws from the transmission system in excess of its reserved service limit (Exceedance Hour), including repeated exceedances (penalty ratchet)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: A penalty rate that is twice the rate the Commission established for FCD transmission service; the text does not state a monetary amount
enforcement.penalty_formula: Two-part framework adopted from Indicated TOs: base penalty charge per Exceedance Hour, calculated as the Hourly Exceedance MW times the Equivalent Hourly FCD rate (FCD rate divided by 8,760) times the number of Exceedance Intervals within the hour; penalty ratchet adds daily, weekly, monthly or annual penalty charges. Penalty revenues are distributed as pro rata bill credits to non-offending transmission customers.
enforcement.penalty_reference: Order No. 890, 118 FERC ¶ 61,119 at P 848 (rebuttable presumption that unreserved use penalties no greater than twice the firm point-to-point rate are just and reasonable)

evidence.quote: a penalty rate that is twice the rate we establish in this order for FCD transmission service
